If sentiment is >0.5 in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for mid-horizon (days 15–25) to align with bullish momentum decay.

If sentiment is <0.3 in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early-horizon (days 1–10) to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.

If forecast exceeds true value by >2.0% in late-horizon (days 26–30), apply downward correction of 1.0–1.5% to avoid overreaction to recent volatility.

If sentiment spikes >0.8 in day 1–3, suppress forecast peak in day 5–7 to prevent overcorrection from sentiment-driven momentum.

If true value dips below 70.0 in late-horizon, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment remains <0.3 to avoid false bullish reversal signals.

If forecast shows upward trend but sentiment is flat or declining, reduce slope by 10–20% in mid-horizon to reflect sentiment lag.
